question: How does Catholic teaching describe the relationship between the Mass and the sacrifice of Calvary?

choices.A: The Mass is a re-presentation (making present again) of the one sacrifice of Calvary — not a repetition or addition
choices.B: The Mass is a separate sacrifice that supplements the incomplete sacrifice of the Cross
choices.C: The Mass is only a symbolic memorial with no sacrificial character
choices.D: The Mass repeats the sacrifice of Christ, increasing the merit available to the Church

teaching.title: The Mass as Re-presentation of Calvary
teaching.body: The Council of Trent defined that the Mass is a 'true and proper sacrifice' but explicitly not a new or additional sacrifice — it is the one sacrifice of the Cross made present (re-presented) sacramentally. Christ does not die again; rather, the same eternal offering that he makes at Calvary is made present across time. This is grounded in Hebrews, which speaks of Christ as priest offering once-for-all while remaining a perpetual intercessor. The Protestant objection ('the Mass adds to the Cross') misses this distinction.
